standard_prerequisites.name: The definition of a constructible set as a finite union of locally closed sets, and the notion of a retrocompact open (an open whose inclusion is quasi-compact)
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Set up in the author's section on constructible sets, immediately before the counted statement
standard_prerequisites.use: Fixes the family whose closure properties the statement asserts and the notion of retrocompactness used in the proof.

core_obligations: Unions and intersections of retrocompact opens: the proof observes that the union of two retrocompact opens is retrocompact because the union of two quasi-compact subsets is quasi-compact, and then shows the same for intersections by checking quasi-compactness of the intersection of a retrocompact open with a quasi-compact open (proof lines 2794-2799).
Complement of a retrocompact open: the proof records that the complement of a retrocompact open is constructible, since it is the intersection of an open with a closed set (proof lines 2799-2803).

Closure properties: combining the three observations gives that constructible sets are closed under finite unions, finite intersections and complements, by writing a constructible set as a finite union of intersections of an open and a closed set (proof lines 2803-2804).
proof_roadmap: 先证两个 retrocompact 开集之并与交仍 retrocompact（用准紧子集之并准紧）。
再指出 retrocompact 开集的补是 constructible（开集与闭集之交）；由「constructible = 有限个开∩闭之并」即得对有限并、有限交与补封闭。
difficulty_reason: The counted statement is the closure of the family of constructible sets under the Boolean operations (author lemma at source lines 2787-2791, label lemma-constructible). The proof (source lines 2793-2805) is a working verification built on retrocompactness: the author shows that unions and intersections of retrocompact opens stay retrocompact, using the quasi-compactness of finite unions of quasi-compact subsets (proof lines 2794-2799), records that the complement of a retrocompact open is constructible (proof lines 2799-2803), and then reads off the three closure properties for constructible sets written as finite unions of open-and-closed intersections. The lemma is the base for the chapter's subsequent results on constructible sets and their images. H2.
